context: It's interesting over in 2 John, just one chapter in that particular epistle, but it says in verse number six, and this is love that we walk after his commandments.
point_summary: Walking in obedience to God's commandments is repeatedly affirmed throughout Scripture as the very definition of love, not its opposite.

context: 2 John and verse number 7, the Bible says this. Notice just a few pages over in 2 John, verse number 7, for many deceivers are entered into the world.
point_summary: Denying that Jesus Christ came in the flesh is the defining mark of a deceiver and antichrist, confirming the sermon's point that false teachers are many and united in rejecting the incarnation.

context: 2 John 8 says that we may receive a full reward.
point_summary: 2 John 1:8 is cited as scriptural warrant for the reality of rewards at the judgment seat, with the phrase "full reward" grounding the sermon's broader discussion of crowns to be received.

point_summary: Because God is love, He gave humanity truth — and 2 John grounds the claim that God's love and His truth are inseparable motivations for revealing Scripture to sinners.

context: we are to walk in love that we're to love one another
point_summary: The New Testament's repeated call to walk in love, including in 2 John, sharpens the heartache of James 4's portrait of division and carnality among believers.

context: Second John this evening, I want you to hold your spot there in the book of Second John
point_summary: Returning to 2 John as a whole after verse-by-verse study, the sermon frames the letter's 13 verses as a unified witness to the believer's deliberate choice of truth.

context: the book of Second John
point_summary: The book of 2 John is reviewed as a whole in this closing message, with John's self-designation as "the elder" in verse 1 anchoring the epistle's authorship and pastoral voice.

context: in the book of 2 John
point_summary: John's self-identification as "the elder" in this epistle frames his authority as an eyewitness and apostle who walked with the living Word, making him a uniquely qualified voice on the theme of truth.

context: look in verses one through three
point_summary: John's unique position as eyewitness, hearer, and recorder of the living Word grounds his authority to write about truth and instruct believers across generations.

context: the elder unto the elect lady and her children, whom I love in the truth. And not I only, but also all they that have known the truth for the truth's sake which dwelleth in us and shall be with us forever
point_summary: John's repeated use of "truth" in the opening verses frames the entire letter around the privilege and responsibility of knowing truth—a gift not universally accessible.

context: Grace be with you, mercy and peace from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father in truth and love
point_summary: Truth's repeated presence in 2 John 1:3 grounds the sermon's opening call to *know* truth, distinguishing mere access to truth from the desire required to actually possess it.

context: the application of what we're dealing with in our passage in 2 John
point_summary: Walking in truth requires both a desire to know it and a daily, diligent return to Scripture, since the living Word speaks distinctly to changing circumstances each time it is read.

context: all they that have known the truth
point_summary: Knowing truth and walking in truth are distinct: 2 John 1:1's phrase "known the truth" sets up a contrast with verse 4's "walking in truth," showing that knowledge must become obedience.

context: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children, what, walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father
point_summary: Walking in truth is distinct from merely knowing truth, as John's joy over the children's obedience in verse 4 illustrates that received commandments must be actively lived out.

context: And now I beseech thee, lady, not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another
point_summary: Walking in truth—not merely knowing it—is the commandment John reiterates from the beginning, as the sermon distinguishes between intellectual knowledge of truth and obedient, active practice of it.

context: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, that as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it
point_summary: Walking in truth—not merely knowing it—is the commandment of 2 John 1:6, as the repeated use of "walk" across verses 4–6 distinguishes intellectual knowledge from obedient, lived application.

context: for many deceivers are entered into the world who confess not that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh
point_summary: Denying that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh marks one as a deceiver and antichrist, making the stand against false teaching inseparable from walking in truth.

context: Look to yourselves that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward
point_summary: Vigilance against false teaching is urgent because spiritual progress already made can be forfeited, making it necessary to stand for truth rather than merely know or walk in it.

context: Whosoever transgresseth and abideth not in the doctrine of Christ hath not God. He that abideth in the doctrine of Christ, he hath both the Father and the Son
point_summary: Abiding in the doctrine of Christ is the dividing line between those who have God and those who do not, making doctrinal fidelity the test of genuine standing before the Father and the Son.

context: If there came any unto you and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him Godspeed
point_summary: Receiving a false teacher into one's home or greeting him makes one complicit in his evil deeds, so standing for truth requires active refusal to extend fellowship to those who deny the doctrine of Christ.

context: For he that biddeth him Godspeed is partaker of his evil deeds
point_summary: Welcoming a false teacher—even with a greeting—makes one a partaker in his evil deeds, so standing for truth requires refusing fellowship with those who deny the doctrine of Christ.

context: Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and ink, but I trust to come unto you and speak face to face that our joy may be full
point_summary: Standing for truth against false teaching is the culminating call of 2 John, where John's promise to speak face to face frames the letter's closing appeal to hold the doctrine of Christ.

context: children of thy elect sister greet thee, amen
point_summary: Standing for truth against false teaching is the sermon's third and climactic movement, anchored in 2 John's closing verses as the necessary response to the doctrinal threats John has just identified.
